decision.summary: The dominant multi-axis step at index 540 (U↓~15, E↑~25, N↑~10) persists through the end of the allowed context (699) with no opposing return observed; thus it cannot be confirmed as temporary. A secondary adjustment near 575 shows smaller co-directional shifts (U↓~5, E↑~5) followed by a minor, axis-asymmetric U uptick (579–584) that does not constitute a return. No interval satisfies the criteria for a confirmed temporary offset (i.e., clear onset, sustained interior, and unambiguous opposing return within allowed context). All candidate intervals remain uncertain.

intervals.observation: U drops sharply ~15 units between 539–540, E jumps ~25 units at 540, N rises ~10 units by 541; all three axes sustain offset through 574 with no return. Interior shows minor fluctuations but no reversal toward pre-event levels. Return not observed within allowed context (ends at 699), and post-574 U/E show secondary step (~−5 U, +5 E) at ~575 without recovery. Onset is abrupt (≤1 day), interior is stable offset, but absence of opposing return prevents confirmation of temporariness.

After secondary adjustment near 575, U continues descending to ~−18 by 577 then stabilizes; E remains elevated. A subtle partial rebound in U begins ~579 and continues to ~584 (U rises ~2 units), but N and E do not reverse. No full return to pre-540 baseline; the small U uptick is isolated and not mirrored in other axes. Not a closed temporary interval.
